taiwanExercise.what: Taiwan, 2023: 82.6% of people 13 and over exercise; 3.64 sessions a week on average; about 35% exercise regularly (the 7-3-3 standard)
taiwanExercise.source: Sports Administration, Ministry of Education, 運動現況調查 2023, as reported by The News Lens (thenewslens.com/article/244223) and NOWnews (nownews.com/news/6348722)

badmintonWeekly.what: recreational badminton players play about twice a week: the most common answer was 2 times a week (Taipei venues, 2005), 2.11 a week on average (Malacca, Malaysia)
badmintonWeekly.source: airitilibrary.com 16808495-200512-x-13-74-87-a (Taipei facility users); Malaysian Orthopaedic Journal 2009 3(2) 'Injuries' (morthoj.org/2009v3n2/Injuries.pdf)

replies.what: about 70% of WhatsApp messages and 44% of Instagram messages answered within five minutes (3.4 million messages, 889 chats)
replies.source: 'Sorry for the late reply: Response times and reciprocity in WhatsApp and Instagram chats', arXiv 2605.03687 (2026)

noShows.what: free events: a median no-show rate of about 28% (32% at events of 10 to 49 people), against 17% for paid ones, over 1,070 events
noShows.source: PheedLoop Event Data Lab Report #05 (pheedloop.com/blog/event-data-lab-report-5): vendor data, not peer reviewed

simulators.what: LLM-simulated users are unreliable proxies: changing the model that plays the user moved agents' success by up to 9 points; non-collaborative users degrade agents
simulators.source: Seshadri et al., 'Lost in Simulation', arXiv 2601.17087 (2026); Shim et al., 'Non-Collaborative User Simulators for Tool Agents', ICLR 2026, arXiv 2509.23124

compare.what: about 70% of WhatsApp messages and 44% of Instagram messages answered within five minutes (3.4 million messages, 889 chats)
compare.source: 'Sorry for the late reply: Response times and reciprocity in WhatsApp and Instagram chats', arXiv 2605.03687 (2026)

replyDelays.reading: 86% of the users' answers to their agent came within five minutes (answers in the chat they were already in, and answers to a push later). The model's own medians (53.5 minutes for the middle persona) are slower than people answering friends; slow answers cost Serve (holds lapse, talks wait) and the baseline (group-chat replies) alike.

notThisWeek.note: No published rate found for turning down a game that fits; the model's numbers are assumptions (personas.mjs).

playFrequency.reading: The personas want fewer games (median 1 a week) than recreational badminton players play (about 2): a conservative choice, since less wanting leaves less for Serve to win.

messages.reading: Character-trigram Jaccard similarity of what each person wrote: one person's messages against another's, and a person's messages against each other.

sensitivity.reading: Baseline: player-games per user over the trial, the mean and the 5th to 95th percentile over 20 seeds. Serve: the games its runs booked, turned up to again under each change (what was booked is not re-run).
